key_insight: A conformal risk control framework can decide when to trust an ML interatomic potential and when to send a configuration to DFT, while guaranteeing the MLIP error on kept predictions stays below a user-set risk level.
engineering_relevance: This lets automated materials screening cut expensive DFT labeling throughput without losing control of prediction quality, improving the efficiency of large-scale structure search and discovery pipelines.
method: Map each structure’s atomic numbers and Cartesian coordinates to a fixed geometric descriptor.
Predict an MLIP–DFT disagreement score for energy and force quantities with a lightweight model.
Use conformal risk control to calibrate a DFT-selection threshold that meets a target error fraction α.
evidence_signal: Across eight dataset–MLIP pairs under the same guarantee, the method sent 7%–14% fewer configurations to DFT than committee baselines at α=0.3, with the biggest gains when DFT labels and MLIP training data used different functionals/basis sets.
watch_item: Performance depends on calibration quality and may narrow when the DFT labels closely match the MLIP training setup, so threshold transfer across domains should be checked carefully.
paper_title: Risk-Controlled DFT Selection for Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials
